UNIT II · LESSON 2.315 min read

Legal Framework for Cyber Crime Investigation

Match each investigative action to a power, its conditions, and its safeguards under the applicable procedural law.

Print / PDF
01

Complaint, production, and search

BNSS section 173 governs information relating to cognizable offences, including specified electronic communication and signature requirements. Section 174 addresses investigation of cognizable cases. Section 94 provides for summoning production of documents or things, including electronic records, subject to its terms and exclusions. These are not interchangeable with a general search authorization.

Section 185 governs searches by police officers under its conditions, including recording grounds and the specified audiovisual documentation of search and seizure. Section 105 adds mandatory audio-video recording for specified searches, with implementation details to be checked. Section 106 concerns attachment of property derived from criminal activity in the situations it covers. Always read the current provision rather than relying only on old CrPC practice.

02

Provider records and interception are different

BNSS section 94 can support an order for necessary documents or things, including electronic records held by a person or intermediary, subject to its conditions and exclusions. Section 69 interception, monitoring, or decryption requires its own competent authorization and the 2009 Rules’ safeguards. Section 69A blocking is not a power to search every device. A request for historical records is not the same as real-time interception.

A subscriber record, traffic metadata, and message content can raise different privacy and statutory concerns. Minimize the request to relevant accounts and dates. Record the recipient, authority, delivery method, response, and verification. Where the provider is overseas, identify the appropriate legal assistance or other lawful route instead of assuming a domestic notice has unlimited reach.

03

Rights, documentation, and exclusion of assumptions

A device search must remain within lawful scope and be conducted with proportionate safeguards. Record the place, people, device state, identifiers, seized accessories, and reasons for each action. Where a person cannot supply a password, do not assume obstruction; self-incrimination, privilege, and the exact legal power require careful analysis. Selvi does not create a blanket answer for all biometric or password demands.

The applicable date determines whether a CrPC or BNSS provision governs, subject to savings. The IT Act and other special laws may add requirements. A legally sound file includes the order or authority, execution record, custody record, and examination report—not merely a forensic tool’s output. An educational checklist is not a warrant or legal advice.

The idea to take with you

Different data and different methods require different powers. Precision at this stage protects both the case and individual rights.
